findings.summary: Whether checks were pending is decided by a fresh read of the checks after the refusal, not by the state at the moment of the refusal, and this adds one extra checks read per rule-violation refusal.
findings.evidence: `self.check_report(head).is_ok_and(|report| report.checks == Checks::Pending)` runs after the PUT fails, and land_pr then reads the checks again. If a check finishes between the refusal and this read, a real pending refusal is left unmarked: the record stays unmarked and D87 can still fire. That is the conservative side, and the D150 Tradeoff section discusses this race. A possible improvement is to reuse land_pr's read, or pass in the pending state already known before the merge, so there is one read and one source of truth.

summary: The candidate does what the retry asked for. It keeps the earlier code fix, and D87's signal now skips a host-error record marked `checks_pending`. The mark is set by `GhClient::merge` on the log entry of its own refused call, found by the id that `HostErrorLog::record` returns. It no longer marks the last logged Merge entry. The decision note is a new final entry, D150, appended after D149. It cites D87 and says pending-check merge refusals no longer fire its signal, and no D87 line is changed. I ran the four named test commands and all pass: watcher 27/27, gh 125/125, athena-data 143/143, and the decisions guard 5/5, including `the_decision_log_is_well_formed_and_only_appended_to`. The new tests would fail without the change. Without the `!error.checks_pending` term, the marked 405 fires D87. Without marking, or marking the wrong entry, the gh assertions on the 405/422 entry fail; the target entry is checked not to be the last one. Old records stay compatible: an old-format record validates and writes back byte-for-byte. The changed files match the deliverables list, and nothing under records/ is touched. The CHANGELOG entry names the pending-check 405 false positive and says existing records/ are untouched. There is one minor finding about how "pending" is decided: by a second read of the checks after the refusal, not the state at the moment of the refusal. The D150 Tradeoff section discloses this, and it can only suppress a firing, never cause a false one.
